extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, assignees, and others submitting assignment/recordation documents to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for preparing, signing, submitting, and processing cover sheets, assignments, licenses, and related recordation documents with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (including paper, facsimile, EPAS electronic submissions, and form usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark cover sheet must include citizenship of conveying party
rubrics_metrics.description: Each trademark cover sheet should include the citizenship of the party conveying the interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as an explicit content requirement for trademark cover sheets (see MPEP § 302.07(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement cover sheet content
rubrics_metrics.description: When seeking to record a joint research agreement or excerpt under § 3.11(c), the cover sheet must identify the document as a 'joint research agreement'; indicate the name of the owner of the application or patent; indicate the name of each other party to the joint research agreement; indicate the date the joint research agreement was executed; and include the signature of the party submitting the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items should be provided in the appropriate spaces if using an Office-provided form (e.g., Form PTO-1595). The cover sheet must clearly identify the document as a joint research agreement and provide its execution date and all parties' names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature format for cover sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: For assignment documents or name changes filed electronically, the person who signs the cover sheet must either: (i) place a symbol comprised of letters, numbers, and/or punctuation marks between forward slash marks (e.g., /Thomas O’Malley III/), or (ii) sign the cover sheet using some other form of electronic signature specified by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) for S-signature rules (composition, placement, practitioner registration number requirements) and acceptable graphic representations for electronic filing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark assignment recipient identification
rubrics_metrics.description: For trademark assignments, the cover sheet must include the entity and citizenship of the party receiving the interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the receiving party is a domestic partnership or domestic joint venture, the cover sheet must set forth the names, legal entities, and national citizenship (or state/country of organization) of all general partners or active members composing the partnership or joint venture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mix patent and trademark information on a cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover sheet should not refer to both patents and trademarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any information submitted with a request for recordation against a trademark application or registration will become public record upon recordation, so patent-related confidential information should not be included on trademark submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cover sheet content for governmental interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Each patent cover sheet seeking to record a governmental interest must indicate that the document relates to a Government interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet must also indicate, if applicable, that the document to be recorded is not a document affecting title (see § 3.41(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of patent assignment cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover sheet for patents or patent applications must contain: (A) the name of the party conveying the interest; (B) the name and address of the party receiving the interest; (C) a description of the interest conveyed or transaction to be recorded; (D) each patent application number or patent number against which the document is to be recorded (or indication that the document is filed together with a patent application); (E) the name and address of the party to whom correspondence concerning the request should be mailed; (F) the date the document was executed; and (G) the signature of the party submitting the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each patent cover sheet should also contain the number of patent applications/patents identified and the total fee. If the assignment is also intended to serve as an oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63, the cover sheet must contain a conspicuous indication of that intent (see MPEP § 302.07(h) and 3.31(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of descriptions of interests to be used on cover sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable descriptions of the interest conveyed or transaction to be recorded include: assignment; security agreement; merger; change of name; license; foreclosure; lien; contract; and joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These example descriptors help identify the nature of the document being recorded on the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cover sheet must not reference trademark filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent cover sheet may not refer to trademark applications or registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate recordation paths/forms should be used for patent versus trademark matters to avoid public disclosure and processing confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO-1595
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO-1595, Recordation Form Cover Sheet, may be used as the cover sheet for recording documents relating to patent(s) and/or patent application(s) in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the Office-provided form helps ensure required fields are completed; joint research agreement identification and party fields map to form spaces as noted in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address for submission of assignment documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and cover sheets submitted by mail for recordation should be addressed to Mail Stop Assignment Recordation Services, Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450, unless they are filed together with new applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests accompanying new applications should be addressed to the Commissioner for Patents at the same P.O. Box address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile (fax) submission permitted with conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments and other documents affecting title may be submitted to the Office via facsimile (fax) into the Patent and Trademark Assignment System; the sender's fax machine should be connected to a dedicated line because recordation notices will be returned automatically to the sending fax number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office system cannot complete transmission of the recordation notice, the notice will be printed and mailed by USPS. Recorded documents will not be returned with the Notice of Recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents not eligible for facsimile submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The following cannot be submitted via facsimile: (A) assignments submitted concurrently with newly filed patent applications; (B) documents with two or more cover sheets (e.g., a single document with separate cover sheets for assignment and license); and (C) requests for 'at cost' recordation services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions must be sent via other permitted channels (mail or electronic filing as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment options and credit card handling for recordation fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the recordation fee may be by credit card (use of Credit Card form PTO-2038 is required to keep the credit card information separate from assignment records) or by a USPTO Deposit Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check current fee schedule on the Office website before submitting; see MPEP § 509 for fee payment details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt for facsimile submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt accorded to an assignment document sent by facsimile transmission is the date the complete transmission is received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits of a certificate of transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-recordable fax submissions returned and resubmission preserves receipt date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document submitted by fax is determined not to be recordable, the entire document, its cover sheet, and the Office 'Notice of Non-Recordation' will be transmitted back to the sender by fax; after corrections, the initial submission, as amended, may be resubmitted by mailing the corrected submission to the address in 37 CFR 3.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely resubmission will provide the sender with the benefit of the initial receipt date as the recordation date in accordance with 37 CFR 3.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent and Trademark Assignment System recordkeeping (reel/frame/stamp)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent and Trademark Assignment System assigns reel and frame numbers and superimposes recordation stampings on processed and stored electronic images; copies of all recorded documents will have the reel and frame numbers and recordation stampings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assures consistent indexing and retrieval of recorded documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPAS (Electronic Patent Assignment System) submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any assignment-related document submitted by EPAS must include an identified application or patent number and one cover sheet to record a single transaction which cover sheet is to be completed online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee for recording an electronically submitted document is currently $0 but customers should check the current fee schedule; signature requirements for electronic filings must comply with 37 CFR 3.31(a)(7) or 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2). Date of receipt is the date the complete transmission is received in the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-recordable EPAS submissions handling and resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document submitted by EPAS is determined not to be recordable, the entire document with its associated cover sheet and the Office 'Notice of Non-Recordation' will be transmitted via fax back to the sender if possible; once corrections are made, the initial submission, as amended, may then be resubmitted by mailing the corrected submission to the address in 37 CFR 3.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission preserves the benefit of the initial receipt date per 37 CFR 3.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recorded assignment on division and continuation applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a division or continuation application, a prior assignment recorded against the original application is applied (effective) to the division or continuation application because the recorded assignment gives the assignee rights to subject matter common to both applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the Office’s assignment records will only reflect an assignment of a division or continuation application if a request for recordation in compliance with 37 CFR 3.28, accompanied by the required fee (37 CFR 3.41), is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment effect for substitute and continuation-in-part applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a substitute or continuation-in-part application, a prior assignment of the original application is not applied (effective) to the substitute or continuation-in-part application because the original assignment gives rights only to subject matter common to both applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute or continuation-in-part applications therefore require the recordation of a new assignment if they are to be issued to an assignee, unless the substitute or continuation-in-part is filed on or after September 16, 2012 and the assignee is the original applicant (see 37 CFR 3.81 and MPEP §§ 307–308).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issuance to assignee rules (37 CFR 3.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may issue in the name of the assignee consistent with the application’s assignment where a request for such issuance is submitted with payment of the issue fee, provided the assignment has been previously recorded in the Office. If the assignment has not been previously recorded, the request must state that the document has been filed for recordation as set forth in § 3.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for issuance in the assignee’s name is submitted after payment of the issue fee, the request must include a request for a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 and the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i), and must state that the assignment was submitted for recordation before issuance. Partial assignee issuance rules and printing practices (only first appearing name printed on the patent where multiple names for same party are listed on PTOL-85B) are described; assignment information printed on a patent is not updated after issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction requirements for assignee name corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 arising from incomplete or erroneous assignee’s name furnished, or a missing assignee’s name, in item 3 of PTOL-85B will not be granted unless a request under 37 CFR 3.81(b) has been granted and the assignment was submitted for recordation as set forth in 37 CFR 3.11 before the patent issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests under 3.81(b) should be directed to the Office of Petitions and include: (A) processing fee per 37 CFR 1.17(i); (B) request for issuance in the name of the assignee or correction; (C) statement that the assignment was submitted for recordation before patent issuance; and (D) request for certificate of correction under 1.323 with fee per 1.20(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants other than the inventor must provide applicant/ownership data and record documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is made by a person other than the inventor under 35 U.S.C. 118/37 CFR 1.46, the application must contain an application data sheet specifying in applicant information the assignee or person showing proprietary interest. If the applicant is the assignee or obligated assignee, documentary evidence of ownership (e.g., assignment, employment agreement) should be recorded no later than the date the issue fee is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant is a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest, such applicant must submit a petition including the fee (1.17(g)), a showing of sufficient proprietary interest, and a statement that making the application is appropriate to preserve the parties' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of change in real party in interest timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a real party in interest has filed an application under 35 U.S.C. 118, the applicant shall notify the Office of any change in the real party in interest no later than payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent such notification, the Office will presume no change and will grant the patent to the real party in interest of record. Requests to change the recorded applicant cannot be filed after patent grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government license rights statement requirement and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a invention was made with Government support under a federal contract, the application and any patents must include the statement: 'This invention was made with government support under (identify the contract) awarded by (identify the Federal agency). The government has certain rights in the invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement: if related applications are referenced in the first sentence(s) of the specification, the Government License Rights statement should follow immediately as the second paragraph; otherwise it should appear as the first paragraph. Providing the information only on a provisional application cover sheet does not satisfy the statutory requirement, which requires inclusion within the specification (35 U.S.C. 202(c)(6)). See 37 CFR 1.77(b)(1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of arbitration awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A written notice of any award by an arbitrator under 35 U.S.C. 294 must be filed in the Patent and Trademark Office by the patentee or the patentee’s assignee or licensee; a separate notice must be prepared for each patent involved and must set forth patent number, names of inventor and patent owner, names and addresses of the parties, and include a copy of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award is modified by a court, a notice of such modification (with the court’s order) must be filed. Any award is unenforceable until the required notice is filed. Notices should be directed to the Office of the Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature composition and practitioner identification
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature must consist only of letters or Arabic numerals (with appropriate spaces and allowed punctuation) placed between single forward slash marks (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/). A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §§ 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(2) must supply his/her registration number as part of the S-signature or immediately below or adjacent to it (the number character '#' may be used only when appearing before a practitioner’s registration number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signer’s name must be presented in printed or typed form preferably immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature so the identity of the signer can be readily recognized. S-signatures may be used for paper, fax, or attachment filings as permitted by 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications regarding papers and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation to the Office of any paper by a party constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 11.18(b). The person inserting an S-signature or graphic signature certifies that the inserted signature is his or her own; a person submitting a document signed by another under S-signature rules must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of these certification provisions may result in sanctions under 37 CFR 11.18(c) and disciplinary action for practitioners (see 11.18(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and modification of Office forms and certification statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides forms for public use; use of forms for purposes other than intended is prohibited and no changes may be made to certification statements on Office forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing text of a form (other than certification statements) may be modified, deleted, or added to only if all text identifying the form as an Office form is removed. Presentation of an Office form with text identifying it as an Office form constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 11.18(b) that the existing text and certification statements on the form have not been altered except as permitted by EFS-Web customization.
